name: git-poison
description: A VS Code extension that blocks a git commit of any file containing a "Poison Pill" string. Placing a pill stops accidental committing of unfinished TODOs, debug statements, secrets, etc. Also provides navigation to pill locations.

commands.title: Git Poison: Jump To Previous Pill
Git Poison: Jump To Next Pill

git-poison.pillString.title: Poison Pill String
git-poison.pillString.description: The string used to indicate a poison pill in the code. This will be inserted by the "Insert Pill" command and be used to detect pills. Warning: If you don't remove old pills before changing this setting, you may accidentally commit them.

git-poison.overrideSecs.title: Override Blocking Timeout (Seconds)
git-poison.overrideSecs.description: Number of seconds after the override blocking command is executed that blocking will be disabled. After this time, the blocking will be re-enabled.

git-poison.showStatusBar.title: Show Status Bar
git-poison.showStatusBar.description: Show a status bar item with pill counts.

git-poison.excludeGlobs.title: Folders/Files to Exclude
git-poison.excludeGlobs.description: Glob patterns to exclude from scanning. Use brace expansion syntax like {folder1,folder2} for multiple folders. Comma-separated patterns are not supported - use brace expansion instead.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.lint:watch: echo 'eslint:watch not used , running eslint extension instead'
